useCase.name: Calculate each employee's monthly pay from their attendance and leave allowance, and get the run approved

intent.name: payroll.run.start

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A future month is refused by the API.

errors.note: Attendance for it does not exist yet.

errors.meaning: The run has already been approved for that month and scope.

planningRules.rule: Never infer the month from today's date. Payroll is usually run for the month just ended, and a planner that assumed the current one has run the wrong month's attendance.
Never repeat a figure back to an actor who cannot see it. Generated salaries are visible only to the Principal and Accounts (BR-9, E9), and the School Admin who starts the run is not one of them.
Never describe starting a run as generating or paying anything. Nothing is calculated until the scope is set, and a salary generated is not a salary paid (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A run is never deleted (BR-13). One opened in error is left unapproved and unreleased, and its record stays.

intent.name: payroll.run.generate
intent.summary: Generate the month's salaries from attendance, for every working employee or for one. One step, and nothing is typed.

request.text: tankhwah ka figure khud daal do

routesElsewhere.note: Pay is calculated from recorded attendance. Nobody types a salary figure into a run, because a typed figure is a figure nobody can trace to a day worked (BR-1).

request.text: kisi ki kaat maaf kar do

routesElsewhere.note: Only the Principal overrides a figure, and every override is recorded against their name with a reason (BR-10).

request.text: tankhwah ada kar do

routesElsewhere.note: Payment is released only after the run is approved (BR-11).

steps.note: One step across the scope. Attendance is read with the off-day calendar applied (BR-3), leave within the allowance is paid and every day beyond it deducted (BR-4), a day absent with no leave request is unpaid (BR-5), and any advance instalment due is recovered (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Employees with no salary in force and no leave allowance are excluded and listed rather than paid on a guess; incomplete attendance does not stop the run and the unmarked days are listed.
plan.atomicity: One write: a generated salary per employee in scope, each with every line of the calculation, together or not at all. Nothing is paid — a salary generated is not a salary paid (BR-11). The figures are visible only to the Principal and Accounts (BR-9). The calculation works from the salary in force for the month being run, not the latest figure: a rise effective in August does not change what July was paid (BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never supply or adjust a figure. Pay is calculated from recorded attendance (BR-1), and a number in a plan is a payment nobody can trace to a day worked.

Never widen the scope to everybody. A correction for one person does not require the whole month to be run again (BR-2), and regenerating everybody replaces every figure Accounts may already have reviewed.
Report the excluded employees by name. They are not paid at all this month (E1, E2) — an exclusion buried in a total is somebody who discovers it on payday.
Report the unmarked attendance days. They are counted as neither present nor absent (E3), and each one is a day somebody may be paid or docked for once it is marked.
Report the advance recoveries and the balances they leave. The instalment is taken automatically (BR-8), and it is money out of a salary the employee is expecting.
Never repeat a figure to an actor who cannot see it. The generated salaries are visible only to the Principal and Accounts (BR-9, E9).
Never describe generated pay as paid. Payment is released only after the run is approved (BR-11).

reversal.statement: A generated salary is never deleted. A wrong figure is corrected before approval, or adjusted afterwards, and both stay on the record (BR-13).

routesElsewhere.note: Where the attendance is wrong, correcting it and regenerating keeps the figure traceable to days worked (BR-1). An override changes the figure without changing what it was calculated from.

request.text: sab ki kaat maaf kar do

routesElsewhere.note: An override is one figure for one employee, recorded against the Principal's name with its own reason (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. Every override is recorded against the Principal's name with a reason — an override nobody can trace is a payment nobody can defend (BR-10).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An override with no reason is refused by the API.

parameters.notes: The figure the Principal is putting in place of the calculated one. Theirs alone — a number a planner produced is a payment nobody decided.

errors.meaning: An override was made with no reason.
errors.note: An override nobody can trace is a payment nobody can defend (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The actor is not the Principal or Director.

errors.note: The run stands and an adjustment is required rather than the released figure being changed (E10).

planningRules.rule: Never supply the figure. It is money into or out of somebody's pay, decided by the Principal (BR-10) — and unlike every other number in this run, it does not come from attendance.
Never compose the reason. It is what defends the payment when anybody asks why this employee was paid differently from the calculation (BR-10).
Prefer correcting the attendance where the attendance is wrong. Regenerating keeps the figure traceable to days worked (BR-1); an override leaves a right number sitting on a wrong calculation.
Never override across several employees in one plan. Each is one figure, one employee, one reason, recorded against the Principal's name (BR-10).
Never override a released run. The run stands and an adjustment is required instead (E10) — the money has gone.

reversal.statement: An override is not undone. A further change is another override row, each with its previous figure and reason (BR-10, BR-13).

steps.note: One step, and it is the one that moves money. The release posts to the ledger (BR-11) and reduces every outstanding advance by the instalment recovered in the run (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A release before approval is refused; a failed ledger posting releases nothing and leaves the run approved and unpaid.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the release, the ledger posting and the advance balances together or not at all. Where the posting fails nothing is released and the run stays approved and unpaid (E8) — there is no half-paid state. After this the figures cannot be changed: an attendance correction approved later requires an adjustment rather than a change to what was paid (E10).

operations.name: payroll.run.release
operations.idempotencyKey: run_id, since a run is released once and a repeat must not pay twice
operations.purpose: Release payment for the approved run and post to the ledger.

parameters.name: run_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No payroll run matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the runs with their month, scope and status.

parameters.notes: The payroll run, resolved from its month and scope.

parameters.name: branch_id

errors.meaning: Payment was released before the run was approved.
errors.note: A salary generated is not a salary paid (BR-11).

errors.notWritten: Nothing released; the run stays approved and unpaid.
errors.note: There is no half-paid state. Report it and let Accounts retry deliberately.

planningRules.rule: Never release an unapproved run. E7 is BR-11 working, and approving it to get past the refusal would move money on figures nobody reviewed.

Never retry a release automatically after a ledger failure. Nothing was released and the run stays approved and unpaid (E8) — a retry that a person did not ask for is a second attempt to pay everybody.
Report the total and the number paid. This is the act that moves money out of the school, and the figure should be said plainly before and after.
Report the advances reduced. The instalment comes out of a salary the employee is expecting, and the balance left is what they still owe (BR-8).
Say that the figures are now fixed. An attendance correction approved after the release requires an adjustment rather than a change to what was paid (E10).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A release is not reversed. The run stands and an adjustment is required (E10, BR-13). The controller must not attempt a compensating call — the money has left.
